issues.text: Death rates were higher in nursing homes than in residential homes. That reflects how ill people already are when they move in.
issues.problem: Causal explanation stated as fact; Shah 2013 reports standardised mortality ratios only and does not test why. LinkedIn adds 'rather than any effect of the home', which the study did not examine.
issues.source_says: The age and sex standardised mortality ratio for nursing homes was 419 (95% CI: 396-442) and for residential homes was 284 (266-302).
issues.replacement: Death rates were higher in nursing homes than in residential homes. This most likely reflects how ill people already are when they move in; the study did not test the reason. (LinkedIn: replace 'The higher figures reflect how ill people already are when they move in, rather than any effect of the home.' with 'The higher figures most likely reflect how ill people already are when they move in; the study did not test the reason.' Apply same hedge in bluesky and threads.)

issues.text: about 1 in 9 nursing home residents, and 1 in 6 in dementia units
issues.problem: 11% applies to regular (ordinary) units only, not to all nursing home residents; LinkedIn states this correctly.
issues.source_says: 11% of the patients in regular nursing home units and 17% of the patients in special care units for people with dementia
issues.replacement: about 1 in 9 residents in ordinary nursing home units, and 1 in 6 in dementia units, (same fix in threads; bluesky: 'about 1 in 9 residents in ordinary units'; visual line: 'In one Norwegian study, 1 in 9 residents in ordinary units had medicines hidden in one week; 4 in 10 cases were recorded.')
